_status: PLACEHOLDER -- schema NOT established, and purpose only inferred
_read_this_first: NOTHING BELOW IS INVENTED. The keys in this file all begin with _ and are prose, not configuration. No field of the real schema is reproduced here, because no artifact in this repository shows one -- and a plausible-looking invented schema is worse than an acknowledged gap, because the next person builds against it.
_this_will_not_start_the_router: This file will NOT satisfy the application. It exists so that `docker compose up` has a real file to bind-mount -- Docker silently CREATES AN EMPTY DIRECTORY at a missing bind source, which would mount a directory onto /app/capability_registry.json and fail as IsADirectoryError far from its cause. Replace the whole object when step 4 of RELEASE-SCOPE.md lands the source that reads it.
_established_from_this_repository: Mounted read-only at /app/capability_registry.json -- deploy/compose.yaml mounts it as a single FILE, not as a directory, because a directory mounted onto /app would shadow the application code.
Read by the application as Path(__file__).parent / "capability_registry.json", so it must land at that exact path (deploy/compose.yaml, deploy/README.md).

Absent from the router build context by design: deploy/images/router/.dockerignore does not re-admit it, and deploy/images/router/Dockerfile note 1 records that the private original baked all four in and the release cannot.
The real file 'describes a specific fleet' -- that sentence in deploy/images/router/Dockerfile note 1 covers all four files together, not this one individually.
_not_established: Everything about the contents. Outside the four-file list, the mount line and the note above, this repository does not mention this file once.
Its relationship to capability_profiles.json, despite the shared prefix.

Whether the word 'capability' here is the same 'capability' as in shared/resolver.py. The registry there tags each endpoint with a required_for value -- core, embeddings, retrieval, arbitration, observability, search -- and deploy/compose.yaml says 'shared/resolver.py records which capability each one unlocks'. Those six labels are the only capability vocabulary in the repository, and NOTHING connects them to this file. They are named here as a lead to check against the real source, NOT as a schema to build against.
_placeholder_rules_for_whoever_fills_thi: Addresses: documentation range only -- 192.0.2.0/24 (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1), or a name under example.com / example.invalid. Never a private address (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16) and never a host name from the private deployment.
Never a credential, key, token or password, not even a placeholder shaped like one. If a field appears to require a real secret, that is a finding, not a value to invent.
Keep the file LF-terminated and ASCII; .gitattributes normalises *.json to LF.
The operator's copy of this file (deploy/config/<name>.json, without .example) is ignored by .gitignore on purpose: it describes a specific fleet.
